newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian bank plans GDR issue on Ukrainian bonds.
newsitem.headline: Russian bank plans GDR issue on Ukrainian bonds.

text.p: Russia's Natsionalny Rezervny Bank plans to issue to foreign investors Global Depositary Receipts representing Ukrainian debt to RAO Gazprom, NRB chairman Alexander Lebedev said.

Lebedev told Reuters his bank had already signed an agreement with a big U.S. investment bank to issue the bonds, but the issue was delayed because a Russian bank bought $400 million of the $800 million issue.
NRB is now in talks with the bank, he said.
NRB is Gazprom's depositary and a trustee on the bonds, he said.
He said the bonds were issued in many kinds of paper making it difficult for foreign investors to deal with them.

"Now these are 40 kinds of bonds, which means each bond of each series with a two, four, five year tenor and each paper split into quarterly paper," Lebedev said. "Foreign investors do not understand so many different papers, that's why we decided to issue a special instrument, which covers Ukrainian paper and is one paper."
Ukraine's total debt to Gazprom is $1.4 billion with a 10-year tenor and a coupon payment of 8.5 percent, he said.
